headlines.title: U.S. Ambassador Huckabee condemns ‘Israeli terrorists’ for siege of West Bank homes
headlines.description: Dozens of Israeli settlers have trapped two Palestinian families in their West Bank homes for days, cutting off food, water and electricity. Their actions even drawing the ire of U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee. The IDF says settlers were dispersed, but some remain. NBC News' Matt Bradley reports from the occupied West Bank.

headlines.title: Parent says son feels a sense of ‘powerlessness’ aboard USS Abraham Lincoln
headlines.description: Growing concerns are emerging over conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln as sailors and families report low morale, supply shortages and months without a port call. In an interview with NBC News’ Tom Llamas, one parent calls for answers, saying her son feels a sense of “powerlessness” while serving aboard the carrier.

headlines.title: Kennedy Center board votes to add president’s name again — and throw in a ‘Trump Plaza’
headlines.description: The board also voted to close the center’s main building for renovations while keeping a smaller addition open in response to a court order.

headlines.title: Custody battle between biological parents and surrogate
headlines.description: The biological parents of a baby boy, born via surrogate, are fighting for custody after the gestational carrier refused to have an abortion when they learned about a serious heart defect at 20 weeks pregnant. Instead, the Alaska based surrogate fled to Texas where she carried the baby to term, and is now fighting for parental rights. NBC News’ Ryan Chandler has the latest.

headlines.title: Ticks that cause Lyme and other diseases have migrated south. Are doctors ready?
headlines.description: New research from the CDC finds that ticks that cause diseases keep marching into new areas.

headlines.title: Witness video of Madison police killing raises questions of why lethal force was used
headlines.description: Local authorities said that the matter is being investigated and that the officers involved have been placed on administrative leave.

headlines.title: Perez Hilton has long road to recovery, had struggled with depression, sister says
headlines.description: Barbara Lavandeira recalled finding her brother in a state of distress on Aug. 4 and said “we remain hopeful” as he recovers.

headlines.title: Selena Gomez and her mom accused of fraud over their mental health startup
headlines.description: Superstar Selena Gomez and her mother are accused of defrauding investors of their mental health startup, Wondermind, in a federal lawsuit filed Thursday.

headlines.title: Judge shows signs of frustration with DOJ attorneys over handling of Epstein files
headlines.description: The judge said he had “absolutely no desire” to go down the road of holding government attorneys in contempt but gave a history lesson on when he has done so.

headlines.title: Appeals court dodges major ruling on Trump’s contentious use of obscure deportation law
headlines.description: The case focuses on last year’s attempted removal of alleged Tren de Aragua gang members using the 18th century Alien Enemies Act.

headlines.title: The Constitution at a standstill: From the Politics Desk
headlines.description: In today’s edition, NBC News reporters dig into the impact of the Iran war on the economy at home and also on U.S. forces deployed in the region.

headlines.title: Haitians in Ohio who lost protected status get ankle monitors instead of ICE detention
headlines.description: The decision is due to a lack of detention space, sources say, and may clash with the White House’s hard-line immigration approach.
